title: Merlin: how editors understand OCaml
body: Editor support for OCaml, such as error squiggles, type-on-hover and jump-to-definition, comes from Merlin. `ocamlmerlin` is a small server that holds a parsed and typed view of a file and answers queries about it. An editor plug-in sends a query, with the buffer on standard input, and receives JSON, so any editor can use it by speaking the same protocol.

You can speak the protocol yourself. `ocamlmerlin single errors -filename example/bad.ml < example/bad.ml` type-checks the buffer and reports each error with its position and message; an empty list means the file is fine. `type-enclosing -position 1:4` asks for the type at a position, which is what powers hover. Merlin reads the project's build settings from a configuration, which Dune generates for you with `dune ocaml merlin dump-config`, so the editor sees the same libraries and flags as the build.

Together with `dune` (build), `opam` (packages), `ocamlformat` (layout), `odoc` (documentation) and `utop` (a better toplevel), Merlin makes up the *OCaml Platform* that the Real World OCaml chapter describes. When your editor shows no information, run Merlin by hand: an error here usually points to a missing library in the build file or a file that Dune does not know about.
challenge: example/bad.ml has a type error, so Merlin reports a typer error. Fix it so Merlin reports no errors for the file, and the type of `answer` at line 1 column 4 is reported as `int`.
projectInstructions: Run `dune build --root . @check` so Dune writes Merlin's configuration, then `ocamlmerlin single errors -filename example/bad.ml < example/bad.ml` before and after your change. Ask for the type at a position with `ocamlmerlin single type-enclosing -position 1:4 -filename example/bad.ml < example/bad.ml`. Edit only example/bad.ml.
question: How does an editor get type information from Merlin?
correct: It sends a query with the buffer on standard input and reads a JSON answer
wrong: It links the Merlin library into the editor and calls it directly
It runs the program and reads the values at run time
reasoning: Merlin is a separate server with a text protocol, which lets every editor use the same analysis.
